title: Research
text:
I work on generative control, at the intersection of generative modeling, control theory, optimization, and reinforcement learning.
The central question behind my research is:

How can a pretrained generative model meet new goals and constraints while retaining the behaviors that make it useful?

A generative model offers a rich distribution of possible outputs or actions. At deployment, we need to turn that distribution into useful decisions: change selected properties, respect constraints, and preserve the ability to keep acting. I study the geometry and control authority of frozen generators, and develop methods for steering and selecting their outputs without retraining the underlying model for each request.

title: Research
text:
Main Research Directions

Geometry of Generative Steering
In Spectral Steering, I study how a requested output change interacts with the local geometry of a frozen diffusion sampler. Request-specific analysis predicts when inverse correction can improve the direction of an edit; damped corrections and relinearization extend the approach to finite changes. The work connects structured generation with inverse problems across visual, audio, motion, and control tasks.
Spectral Steering — Under review


Safe Generative Control and Viability
In Certify, Then Select, I study how frozen diffusion policies can respond to constraints absent from their demonstrations. CAST certifies candidate action chunks before ranking them for task performance. CAST-V and CAST-VL account for policy-conditioned viability: whether the policy will still be able to produce safe continuations after the current action. This connects safety certification with the control authority available through finite sampling.
Certify, Then Select — Under review · Project & video


Learning and Adaptation Beyond Demonstrations
I also investigate how diffusion and flow policies, vision-language-action models, and generative dynamics models can support exploration and adaptation. My earlier work on VLA-guided reinforcement learning and generative in-context dynamics learning complements runtime control by studying how agents use prior knowledge and improve through interaction.


Robotics as a Testbed
Robotic manipulation, motion generation, and dynamical systems provide concrete settings in which goals, constraints, and model limitations interact. My work combines theoretical analysis with simulation and real-world robot learning, connecting generative methods to closed-loop decisions and physical task performance.

title: Angelo Moroncelli
text:
Ph.D. Researcher — Generative Control & Robot Learning
IDSIA USI–SUPSI · Lugano, Switzerland
I study generative control: how pretrained generative models can meet new goals and constraints at deployment. My work connects generative modeling, control, optimization, and reinforcement learning, with robotics as a central application.
My recent research asks how to steer frozen diffusion generators through their local geometry, and how to select safe, useful actions from generative policies while preserving their future ability to act. More broadly, I investigate how generative priors can support adaptation, exploration, and learning beyond demonstrations.

title: Angelo Moroncelli
text:
Research Interests


Generative Control
Turning pretrained generative models into controllers that meet new goals and constraints at run time.


Geometry of Steering
Local inverse geometry, controllability, and structured edits of frozen diffusion generators.


Safety & Viability
Certified action selection and preserving a generative policy’s future safe control authority.


Learning Beyond Imitation
Generative priors, reinforcement learning, and adaptation for robot manipulation and embodied decision-making.

title: Angelo Moroncelli
text:
Current Position
I am a Ph.D. researcher at IDSIA USI–SUPSI in Lugano, Switzerland, where I work on Generative AI for Robotic Systems.
I am supervised by Prof. Loris Roveda, with Prof. Alessandro Giusti and Prof. Luca Gambardella as advisors.

title: About
text:
I am a Ph.D. researcher at IDSIA USI–SUPSI in Lugano, Switzerland, where I work on Generative AI for Robotic Systems.
My research focuses on generative control: steering pretrained generative models toward new goals and constraints, and understanding when their outputs can support reliable decisions. I connect local inverse geometry, safe action selection, and policy-conditioned viability with reinforcement learning and robotics.
My background is in automation, control, machine learning, and robotics. I received my M.Sc. and B.Sc. degrees in Automation Engineering from Politecnico di Milano. During my M.Sc., I was a visiting researcher at IRIDIA, Université Libre de Bruxelles, where I worked on SLAM for swarms of robots.
